**Current behavior**
When listening to a native event such as `(window:mousemove)` the component is marked for check. 

**Expected behavior**

> When using OnPush detectors, then the framework will check an OnPush component when any of its input properties changes, when it fires an event, or when an observable fires an event

**Note:** It says that the angular will only check it if an input changes, it fires an output, or an observable fires an output. I can see how this could be considered an `observable` but I wouldn't think of a native event as `observable`.

**Minimal reproduction of the problem with instructions**
https://plnkr.co/edit/CEDANBqgbbKkBHSkHnDk?p=preview

**What is the motivation / use case for changing the behavior?**
If a component wants to listen to a native event it has to manually listen to that event using browser apis if it wants to avoid the change detector. This isn't great.

issue.title: Moving the pointer on the Chart triggers changes
issue.body:
**I'm submitting a ...** (check one with "x") ``` [ X] bug report => search github for a similar issue or PR before submitting [ ] feature request [ ] support request => Please do not submit support request here ``` **Current behavior** Moving the pointer on the Chart triggers changes on any of the parent component variables **Expected behavior** Should not trigger changes **Reproduction of the problem** https://embed.plnkr.co/pDnNlL0nJCsQD6DnxibX/ Open the console on the above Plunkr and then move your mouse over the chart. The console goes logging the number 1 which is a function of a variable (object) that is echoed in the template of the component that uses the ngx-charts. More specifically: ``` @Component({ selector: 'my-app', template: `
{{ obj.test() }}
` }) ``` Where as you can see `
{{ obj.test() }}
` -> `obj` is just another variable in the component with `test` a function that logs `1` to the console. This can relate to all the performance issues reported here. **What is the motivation/use case for changing the behavior?** By always triggering on change this chops the performance dramatically. I want to disable this behavior and this cannot be disabled with any ChangeDetectionStrategy or so. * **ngx-charts version:** 5.3.1 * **Angular version:** 2-4 * **Language:** [all]
